move.subject: Re: Quote from Dichtungswerk Ravensteiner GmbH: Ravensteiner cuts the seal allocation
move.body:
Dear Sir or Madam,

Thank you for your offer and for explaining your position.

Our data shows a different picture on some points:
Our last 3 orders for this part were at EUR 29.89 per unit (po:4500014436-10, po:4500014383-10, po:4500014337-10).
Your rolling scorecard shows on-time delivery of 79.5% (sc:70410@2026Q3).
Our demand forecast for this part has risen 10.1% (fc:340010@2026-09).

Please find our proposal below.

We look forward to your reply.

Kind regards
Purchasing
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH

move.text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

We have reviewed your offer and can adjust our Angebot as follows. We checked the delivery record data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation. We checked the price history data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation. We checked the volume change data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation. Historical pricing is no longer applicable, and maintaining a 54-day lead time is necessary to ensure schedule adherence and improve delivery performance. We can accommodate your increased volume of 23400 units per year, provided the contract remains at 12 months. Under these terms, we propose a revised price of EUR 31.90 per unit. Our price reflects our costs; our calculation stays internal. 

Our current offer stands at a price of €33.80 per unit, Lieferzeit 42 days, a volume of 23400 pcs per year, a contract term of 36 months. Our Lieferzeit is 42 days.

Alternatively, with Lieferzeit 54 days, a volume of 19890 pcs per year and a contract term of 12 months: a price of €31.90 per unit.

This Angebot remains valid for 30 days.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Monika Zellner
Segment Manager, Dichtungswerk Ravensteiner GmbH

decisions.tactician: o3 and o4 give our lowest C (€1,416,340), well below E0 (€1,449,940), because they restore the 42 d contractual lead time at the same price. Option o5/o6's 35 d lead time gives no further C gain and would strain a capacity-tight supplier. I chose o4 over o3 because a 36-month binding commitment gives the supplier what it says it prioritises. That improves our chance of acceptance and secures supply beyond our horizon at no cost to our C. The price is still above the health price, so the relationship margin is safe. a4 anchors on today's €29.89, a2 shows its poor delivery, and a3 signals volume growth it can only win by committing. I left out should-cost (a1) to avoid pushing toward an unhealthy margin.

decisions.tactician: E0, o3, o5 and o6 tie for the lowest C (€1,470,518), well below accepting offer:70410-1 (€1,597,721). E0 keeps the 36 months and 42 d lead the supplier already put on its own sheet and gives it the long commitment it says it prioritises, so it is the most acceptable of the four. o5 and o6 add a 35 d lead it has resisted. The 56 d options cost us more, and o7 costs far more. Citing should-cost backs the price gap. It is too early to accept: the sheet is not a final offer and we have many messages left.
